motivo: A normal day: a debate about declaring the use of AI in the general group, two agent-programming news items in Vibe Coding Educativo and one on imaging in EduMedia-IAG. The rest (Relleu Obert, Buzz, Eduvers, the steam engine with Codex) had already been published.

piezas.titular: Declaring AI use: a teacher asks schools to clarify which uses are acceptable
piezas.entradilla: A teacher asks whether schools, very focused on detecting AI-generated work, explain clearly enough which uses are acceptable and how to declare them.
cuerpo: The usual debate in schools is how to detect work done with AI. In ChatGPT-IA-edu, a teacher proposed shifting it towards transparency of the process, based on [“Verdad a medias: ¿hay que declarar cómo hemos utilizado la IA?”](https://profechef.substack.com/p/verdad-a-medias-hay-que-declarar) (“A half-truth: do we have to declare how we have used AI?”), an instalment of his series “Familias con inteligencia”. Its author is [Chema Falcó](https://profechef.substack.com), a secondary and sixth-form teacher; the paper has already reported on other instalments of the series, on [homework done with AI](pieza:2026-11-01/familias-deberes-ia) and on [the percentage given by a detector](pieza:2026-11-08/detector-ia-no-es-prueba).

The instalment starts from two first-year Bachillerato students, Laura and Pablo, on a piece of work in which AI may be used if it is declared. Laura used it for ideas and to check requirements, but her report presents the work as individual; Pablo declared minimal use and later admitted that he had relied on it extensively. According to the author, the cases serve to work with students on academic integrity, authorship, responsibility and the traceability of learning, and he argues that declaring does not detract from merit but makes authorship verifiable. He proposes a three-sentence template (“I used AI to…”, “Afterwards I verified…”, “The research and the writing were mine”) and points to the INTEF guide, which includes a model declaration.

In the group, the author added the underlying question for schools and teachers: whether it is being explained clearly enough which uses are acceptable, which are not and how they should be declared. He is concerned, he said, that students who want to do the right thing perceive that declaring may count against them. The message ended by asking whether a declaration of AI use is required and of what kind; there is no record of the group replying that day.
The same idea of declaring permitted uses and asking for evidence of the process is the one put forward in [Sunday’s feature on AI detectors](pieza:2026-11-14/detectores-ia-evaluar-proceso).

piezas.titular: Chrome publishes Modern Web Guidance 1.0, a guide to the current web for coding agents
piezas.entradilla: The guide brings together expert-verified solutions and compatibility data to correct the outdated knowledge of models.
cuerpo: In Vibe Coding Educativo it was mentioned that models that generate code may be trained on outdated web development and infrastructure data. As a possible remedy, [Modern Web Guidance 1.0](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/modern-web-guidance-v1) was shared, published on 10 November by Chrome for Developers.

According to the article, it includes an expanded base of guides with cross-browser solutions, each reviewed by experts, and compatibility data based on Baseline. It adds a modernisation workflow that analyses existing code (HTML, CSS, JavaScript and package.json) in search of safe improvements; in this first version, with static analysis of a limited number of patterns. It also offers a public evaluation dashboard that compares results with and without the guide. It is installed with `npx modern-web-guidance@latest install`, or from the agent plugin marketplaces such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. Firefox and Edge join Chrome in supporting the project.

In the group, one person passed the article to an AI assistant, which recommended consulting the documents but not installing the program in case it sends data to Google. The article does not mention what data it does or does not send, so that warning could not be confirmed. Another person said that their assistant had suggested the same thing and an alternative: downloading the documentation as .md files and adding it to the project folder or as an agent skill.
piezas.comprobado: Article opened: components, installation (npx and the Claude Code, Codex and Cursor marketplaces), date (10-11-2026), limited static analysis, public dashboard and that Firefox and Edge join Chrome. “The project was born at Chrome” removed from the draft, which the article does not say. The article does not mention telemetry; the warning about data sharing remains unconfirmed. Messages #15015, #15019 and #15020 (embed of #15015 opened). No earlier pieces on the subject in the paper. English version of the article checked with WebFetch (10 November 2026).
piezas.ilustracion_alt: Three boxes joined by arrows: a file with a clock, labelled “Old data”, an open book guide, labelled “Current web guide”, and a code file with a red tick, labelled “Current code”.

piezas.titular: Antigravity adds Gemini 4 Hydrogen and an Orchestrator mode that shares out the work
piezas.entradilla: Orchestrator combines Hydrogen with more powerful models; access depends on Google’s paid plan.
cuerpo: A member of Vibe Coding Educativo said they still had to try the Orchestrator mode of [Google Antigravity](https://antigravity.google/blog/gemini-4-hydrogen-in-google-antigravity), announced on 12 November together with Gemini 4 Hydrogen.

According to Google, Hydrogen is for everyday programming and agent tasks, with four reasoning levels (low, medium, high by default and a new “xhigh”). Orchestrator is an option in the model drop-down that combines it with more powerful ones, such as [Gemini 4 Carbon](pieza:2026-10-28/gemini4carbon): Carbon explores and plans, Hydrogen edits and tests, and Carbon takes over again if Hydrogen gets stuck. These are the company’s figures: in its Terminal-Bench 4.1 test, Orchestrator comes close to Carbon’s success rate with 24% less quota and 19% less time on average.

Hydrogen is rolling out gradually to the paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscriptions. Orchestrator with Carbon or with Argon is for Google AI Ultra, and Orchestrator with Argon also for paid Google AI Pro. Businesses can access both with Gemini for business. The paper reported on 29 October that Carbon was presented only for cybersecurity specialists; the Antigravity page does not explain how this has been widened, so it is worth checking in the tool itself what each plan offers.

piezas.titular: Seedream 5.5 promises to keep an image stable across 100 rounds of editing
piezas.entradilla: ByteDance presents a version of its image generator designed for retouching the same image again and again without changing what is left untouched, and which generates transparent backgrounds.
cuerpo: ByteDance Seed presented [Seedream 5.5](https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/more-realistic-images-more-stable-editing-across-100-rounds-introducing-seedream-5-5) on 9 November, which was shared in EduMedia-IAG. According to the company, it preserves unedited areas at pixel level and reduces colour shifts and loss of detail, allowing work to continue on the same image for up to 100 rounds of editing; its demonstration chains 100 edits on the same image.

The second novelty is native image generation with an alpha channel, with full and partial transparency, so there is no need to remove the background separately. It may be useful for preparing characters and elements for classroom materials. ByteDance adds improvements in light, skin and materials, and in text within the image; these are figures from its own evaluation, with no details of sample or method.

The page links to access via Dola and the BytePlus Playground, but gives no rollout schedule or says in which regions it will be available, so its availability in Europe is not confirmed. It also announces a Pro version of the series, with no date.
piezas.comprobado: Official post opened: date (09-11-2026), 100 rounds, alpha channel, improvements and evaluation figures (the company’s), access (Dola and BytePlus Playground), Pro version with no date, no regions or schedule. Headline shortened (the draft’s was over 90 characters). “On the image of a person” removed, as it does not appear in the source. No earlier pieces on Seedream.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: Under the title “Seedream 5.5”, an image passes through circular arrows, labelled “100 rounds”, and comes out the same as it went in. On the right, a blue circle on a background of alternating squares, labelled “Transparent background”.

breves.texto: According to the Financial Times, reported by Deseret News, Spotify is preparing for early 2027 a paid add-on ($4 to $5 a month, according to that report) to create AI remixes and covers, with agreements with Universal, Merlin and Believe. Spotify has confirmed neither date nor price; in August it had already announced the project with Universal and Merlin.
Intelética, IBERAMIA’s open-access journal on artificial intelligence, ethics and society, accepts articles in Spanish, Portuguese and English.
